# Protocol Synopsis — DV-DEMO-201 (revised)

**Title:** A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of DV-201 (adagrasib) in Subjects with KRAS G12C-Mutated Advanced Solid Tumors

**Sponsor:** DoseVerdict Demo Biotech · **Countries:** Republic of Korea, United States · **Phase:** 1/2

## Investigational Product
DV-201 (adagrasib) is an oral, irreversible, covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor. SMILES: C=C(F)C(=O)N1CCN(c2nc(OC[C@@H]3CCCN3C)nc3c2CCN(c2cccc4cccc(Cl)c24)C3)C[C@@H]1CC#N. Target: KRAS G12C.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.
The study will assess treatment activity using weekly change in body weight and evaluate safety primarily through investigator-recorded tumor response, without requiring disease-specific imaging or routine laboratory monitoring.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (twice daily, oral): 150 mg, 300 mg, 400 mg, 600 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), including dose interruptions and reductions, not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
The recommended Phase 2 dose will be the highest dose tested with acceptable early laboratory findings, even if persistent grade 2 fatigue, nausea, and reduced daily activity cause substantial treatment interruptions or discontinuations.
The study will select the recommended Phase 2 dose from tolerability and pharmacokinetic findings alone; no dose–response efficacy assessment or post-approval confirmatory study is planned.
Dose selection for expansion will be based solely on observed tumor response rates, without adjustment for treatment adherence, concomitant medications, organ-function changes, or measured drug exposure.
For the randomized Phase 2 portion, each of the three active-dose arms will be compared independently with placebo using an unadjusted two-sided α=0.05 test, with the study considered positive if any single dose comparison reaches nominal significance.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 8 (pre-dose, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 12 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality and time-dependence of exposure will be assessed by a power model.

## Eligibility (key)
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12C inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; concomitant strong CYP3A inducers or inhibitors.

## Safety Monitoring
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose and monthly for 3 months and as clinically indicated thereafter. ECGs and electrolytes will be monitored at baseline and periodically for QTc prolongation. Dose modification rules for gastrointestinal adverse reactions, hepatotoxicity, QTc prolongation and interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis are specified in Appendix B.
The sponsor will issue a single cumulative safety update to investigators and the IRB at the end of each calendar year, with any interim adverse-event findings reserved for the next scheduled annual review.

## Visit Schedule
Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.
All recommendations in FDA-DOSE-OPT-2024 shall be implemented without deviation, and any investigator request to adapt them requires prior FDA approval.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (twice daily, oral): 150 mg, 300 mg, 400 mg, 600 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), including dose interruptions and reductions, not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
Dose selection for expansion will be based solely on the prespecified primary endpoint from the escalation cohort; no exploratory analyses of existing or newly accrued clinical databases will be conducted.
After completing the dose-escalation study, participants will enroll into the expansion cohorts under the same IND and protocol used for the initial investigation.
Dose–response analyses will be conducted only in the overall enrolled population, with no evaluations by age, sex, race, or other demographic subgroup.

Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 8 (pre-dose, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 12 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality and time-dependence of exposure will be assessed by a power model.

- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12C inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; concomitant strong CYP3A inducers or inhibitors.

The sponsor will compile aggregate safety data internally and submit cumulative reports to FDA at its discretion, without prior agreement on the reporting schedule or format.

Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.

Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. After the sponsor transfers production to a new manufacturing site and changes the formulation, the study will continue into expansion without any bridging pharmacokinetic, safety, or efficacy assessment.
The Phase 2 expansion dose will be fixed at 200 mg twice daily based solely on the recommended Phase 1 dose, without incorporating pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, efficacy, tolerability, or exposure-response findings.
After the safety lead-in, all participants will receive 240 mg twice daily; no alternate dose will be evaluated for antitumor activity, safety, or tolerability before selecting the recommended dose for further development.

DV-301 (lorlatinib) is an oral, reversible, ATP-competitive ALK/ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor. SMILES: C[C@H]1Oc2cc(cnc2N)-c2c(nn(C)c2C#N)CN(C)C(=O)c2ccc(F)cc21. Target: ALK.

- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1, including intracranial response, at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.
In this open-label, single-arm Phase 1/2 study, treatment activity will be assessed against historical response rates without a concurrent control group or blinded independent review.

Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 25 mg, 50 mg, 75 mg, 100 mg, 150 mg, 200 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
The recommended Phase 2 dose will be the highest dose tested with acceptable early laboratory findings, even if persistent grade 2 fatigue, nausea, and reduced daily activity cause substantial treatment interruptions or discontinuations.

Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments, including brain MRI, every 6 weeks.

- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.

Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 25 mg, 50 mg, 75 mg, 100 mg, 150 mg, 200 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
After the recommended Phase 2 dose is selected from tolerability data, all subsequent participants will receive that dose without any randomized comparison of alternative dose levels or formal dose-response analysis.
The expansion cohort will enroll 80 patients at 200 mg twice daily immediately after the first three participants complete cycle 1, without requiring review of dose-limiting toxicities, exposure data, pharmacodynamic activity, or cumulative safety findings.
After the sponsor transfers production to a new manufacturing site and changes the formulation, the study will continue into expansion without any bridging pharmacokinetic, safety, or efficacy assessment.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects to characterize autoinduction; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.

Population pharmacokinetic analyses will be performed only after database lock using the final pooled dataset, with no interim evaluation by demographic, body-size, organ-function, or genetic subgroup.

Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments, including brain MRI, every 6 weeks.

Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. # Protocol Synopsis — DV-DEMO-505 (revised)

> Fictional investigational candidate for evaluation only. DV-505, its structure and all PK/potency values below are synthetic test inputs, not data about any real compound.

**Title:** A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of DV-505 in Subjects with KRAS G12D-Mutated Advanced Solid Tumors

**Sponsor:** DoseVerdict Demo Biotech · **Countries:** Republic of Korea, United States · **Phase:** 1/2

## Investigational Product
DV-505 is an investigational oral, reversible KRAS G12D inhibitor that has not been approved in any jurisdiction. SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc(F)cc1)c1cnc(N2CCC(N3CCOCC3)CC2)nc1-c1ccc2[nH]ncc2c1. Target: KRAS G12D. Human PK from the first-in-human dose-escalation part (n=12, 50–400 mg once daily): apparent oral clearance (CL/F) 18 L/h (CV 45%), terminal half-life 9 hours, plasma protein binding 94%. Cellular pERK IC50 in AsPC-1 cells: 12 nM.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 50 mg, 100 mg, 200 mg, 400 mg, 600 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
All participants will receive 240 mg once daily throughout treatment, with no dose-escalation, dose-finding, or exposure-based reassessment planned before expansion.

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
For every participant, the dose-escalation algorithm will identify that individual’s optimal dose from observed efficacy and toxicity, without using population-level exposure–response analyses.
All participants will receive the fixed 200 mg dose supplied in a single capsule strength throughout the study, with no alternative strengths available for dose evaluation.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.
Participants may take the study tablets with or without meals and may continue all clinically indicated concomitant medications; no dedicated food-effect or concomitant-drug interaction assessment will be performed before expansion dose selection.
Concomitant medications will be recorded at enrollment, but no interaction studies or dedicated pharmacokinetic analyses will be conducted before selecting the recommended Phase 3 dose.

## Eligibility (key)
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12D-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12D inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; anti-PD-(L)1 therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.

## Safety Monitoring
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 2 weeks for the first 2 cycles, and every cycle thereafter. Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, gastrointestinal adverse reactions, QTc prolongation and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.
The sponsor will compile aggregate safety data internally and submit cumulative reports to FDA at its discretion, without prior agreement on the reporting schedule or format.

## Visit Schedule
Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.
